title: Lantern: Model & Route Timeline + Token Stack UX and Chart Specs
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Goal: Design a compact, scalable UX pattern (Lantern) that surfaces per-route and per-model performance across three coordinated layers: request lifecycle timeline, token-origin stacked area, and a kernel-selection / execution heatmap. Deliver high-fidelity chart specs and an interactive prototype for PM/ENG review, focusing on latency, throughput, token composition, and cost attribution.
deliverables: Chart-spec doc with rendering rules, color tokens, binning logic, and exportable CSV mappings
Interaction spec: hover, brush, zoom, compare model variants, and token-origin drilldown
Hand-off bundle for frontend (SVG + CSS tokens) and a small design QA checklist
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates coordinated highlighting between timeline, token-stack and heatmap
Token-origin stack breaks down generated tokens into: prompt, context, tool-output, model-generated and cached
Latency timeline annotates stages: routing, queueing, kernel-exec, kv-lookup, token-emit and total-p95/p50 lines
Throughput corridor shows requests/sec with 25/75 and 5/95 quantile ribbons
Cost layer overlays token cost per time bin and allows toggling between unit-cost and aggregated cost
Edge-case: graceful collapse into microtile for small widths (<440px) maintaining key metrics
design_notes: Principle: readable at-a-glance for SREs and PMs; interact to reveal developer-centric microtraces
Use adaptive binning: auto-choose time bucket size based on span length to keep ~40-80 points
Token-stack uses area stacking with subtle strokes; priority on clear color separation for token origins
Heatmap rows order by kernel type then model size to surface scheduling hotspots
Include toggle to normalize per-request vs absolute counts for token-stack comparisons
chart_specs: Timeline (top): horizontal time axis, stacked event bars per request, overlaid p50/p95 latency lines; tooltip shows microtrace link and breakdown of sub-stage durations

Token-Stack (middle): stacked area by token-origin with legend; binning aligned to timeline; deployable color tokens: #2B7A78 (prompt), #FFB86B (context), #7C4DFF (tool-output), #1F8EF1 (generated), #A3A3A3 (cached)
Throughput Corridor (under timeline): smoothed line for median RPS, shaded bands for 25/75 and 5/95 quantiles; allow smoothing window selection (1m/5m/15m)

Execution Heatmap (bottom): X axis time bins, Y axis kernel/instance rows; cell intensity = average exec-time per-token; cell tooltip includes model version, instance id, avg latency, and kernel config
Cost Overlay: optional semi-opaque layer on timeline using per-bin token-cost; hover shows cost breakdown and estimated monthly run-rate extrapolation
interactions: Hover on any layer highlights corresponding time window across all layers and pins a combined tooltip
Brush on timeline to zoom; token-stack and heatmap re-bin to selected window using adaptive binning rules
Click token-origin slice to filter requests that contributed >= X% of tokens (configurable threshold)
Compare toggle: show side-by-side lanes for two model versions or routes for A/B rollouts
Export: CSV of visible time bins with columns: time_start, time_end, requests, tokens_total, tokens_by_origin, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, cost_usd
tradeoffs: Stacked-area vs stacked-bars: chosen area for smoother long-window trends; bars considered but visually noisy for dense timelines
Adaptive binning simplifies UX but complicates front-end implementation and QA (needs canonicalization for CSV exports)
Heatmap row density: limiting to top-12 kernel rows avoids clutter; allow expand to full list to satisfy SRE needs
Color choices prioritize accessibility (contrast ratios) which reduces palette variety; small risk of less distinct hues for many token types
